payout_quote: There is a five cent deposit on carbonated soft drink, beer, malt beverage, and sparkling water containers sold in Massachusetts. / Under the "Bottle Bill," retailers are required to redeem containers at full deposit value, while redemption centers may deduct processing fees from refunds.
steps: Buy eligible beverages in Massachusetts (5¢ deposit at checkout)
Keep clean, empty deposit bottles/cans with deposit labels
Return to a retailer that sells them (redeems at full value) or a redemption center (may deduct processing fees)
catches: This returns YOUR OWN deposit money paid at purchase — it is recovering your own money, not new income.
Only containers bought in-state with the correct deposit label are redeemable; out-of-state containers are ineligible and redeeming them is fraud.
Redemption centers (not retailers) may legally deduct processing fees from your refund; only carbonated beverages are covered — water, juice, wine are excluded.
biggest_catch: Returns your own 5¢ deposit — you paid it at purchase. This is deposit recovery, not income.
eligibility: Anyone who purchased deposit containers in Massachusetts.

c1.evidence: Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection; mass.gov official page.

c3.evidence: No fee to redeem; deposit already paid at purchase.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: buy, save, return to retailer/center, get refund.

notes: MA covers only carbonated beverages — narrower than most bottle-bill states; fraud crackdowns target out-of-state redemptions.
